extracted.intended_audience: high-school students and teachers preparing for the AP English Literature and Composition exam
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for administering, taking, and scoring the AP English Literature and Composition exam (digital format), including section formats, question types, weighting, and expectations for free-response responses and student-selected texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic scoring of free-response questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The free-response questions will be scored using analytic rubrics, rather than the previous holistic rubrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A downloadable document — “AP English Literature and Composition Rubrics with Decision Rules and Scoring Notes” — features general scoring criteria that apply to each of the three free-response questions, regardless of specific question prompt. (The page directs users to download that PDF for the scoring details and decision rules.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Section I — Multiple-Choice format and weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: Section I: Multiple Choice — 55 Questions | 1 Hour | 45% of Exam Score. Includes 5 sets of questions with 8–13 questions per set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each set is preceded by a passage of prose fiction, drama, or poetry of varying difficulty. The multiple-choice section will always include at least 2 prose fiction passages (this may include drama) and at least 2 poetry passages. Test-takers should be prepared to read passages and answer a cluster of questions per passage within the timed section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section II — Free-Response format, categories, and weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: Section II: Free Response — 3 Questions | 2 Hours | 55% of Exam Score. Students write essays responding to three free-response prompts from specified categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three categories are: (1) a literary analysis of a given poem; (2) a literary analysis of a given passage of prose fiction (this may include drama); and (3) an analysis that examines a specific concept, issue, or element in a work selected by the student. Responses are subject to the analytic rubrics referenced on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student-selected work guidance for Question 3
rubrics_metrics.description: When responding to Question 3, students should select a work of fiction that will be appropriate to the question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A general rule is to use a work that is similar in quality to those they have read in their AP class(es). (This is guidance for choosing a text students are prepared to analyze effectively under timed conditions.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of exam structure and difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: The AP English Literature and Composition Exam has consistent question types, weighting, and scoring guidelines every year, and there will be a consistent range of difficulty in the reading passages across all versions of the exam from year to year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an expectation about predictability and comparability across administrations — teachers and students can rely on stable formats and difficulty ranges when preparing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital delivery and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a fully digital exam. Students complete multiple-choice and free-response questions in the Bluebook testing app, with all responses automatically submitted at the end of the exam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students and teachers are directed to download the Bluebook app and log in with College Board account information to access test previews for the digital AP Exams and to practice in the testing environment ahead of exam day.
